rationale: Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲍⲁⲗⲟⲏⲧ. The element ⲍⲁⲗⲟⲏⲧ is unattested in our glossary; possible analyses: (a) Lyc. reflex on ϩⲣⲟϣ-ϩⲏⲧ 'long-suffering' (cf. ϩⲁⲣϣ̄- root); (b) related to ϩⲁⲣⲱⲟⲩ 'be still, quiet'; (c) compound on ϩⲁⲗⲟⲩ 'youth/tenderness' + ϩⲏⲧ 'heart.' Context (the Apostle's manner of replying to the troubled disciple) demands a noun for kindly/gentle disposition. Translating 'gentleness'; awaits parallel confirmation.

Substantival noun used three times in this kephalaion (lines 29, 30, 32) in immediate semantic field of ⲉⲡⲓⲧⲓⲙⲓⲁ 'rebuke' and ϫⲡⲓⲟ 'reprove.' Etymology uncertain: possibly from ϣⲱⲡ/ⲛⲟⲩϣⲡ 'what is needful, fitting' (cf. Crum 567), or a Lyc. reflex of a corrective-speech verb. The text identifies the righteous wrath itself as the ⲛⲟⲩϣⲡ — confirms a juridical-disciplinary noun.

Unclear collocation in line 15. ⲍⲱⲟ̄ⲙ̄ possibly qualitative on ϩⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'tread upon, oppress' yielding 'is afflicted'; ϩⲃ̄ⲓⲁϩ unidentified — possibly Lyc. for ϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'works' or a sufferings/changes-noun. Context (the unrepentant brother's fate before falling into the place of judgment) supports a state-of-misery reading. Confidence low; flag for parallels.

proposed_english: I encompass her / I shall surround her
rationale: 1sg conjunctive ⲛ̄(ⲧⲁ)-ⲕⲱⲛⲧ + 3sg.f object on the encompassing-verb ⲕⲱⲛⲧ̄ (in glossary as 'encompass/surround,' Lyc. for ⲕⲱⲛⲥ̄). The disciple's act of fraternal embrace toward an erring brother/sister, distinct from ⲕⲱⲛⲥ̄ 'pierce/rebuke.'
